target_claim: Whenever the ratios $a_i b_i^{-1}$ agree on parts of $\pi\wedge\sigma$, the equations $u_i v_i=a_i b_i^{-1}$, with $u$ constant on parts of $\pi$ and $v$ constant on parts of $\sigma$, have exactly $|G|^{|\pi\vee\sigma|}$ solutions.
source_quote:
This is zero unless the ratios
$a_ib_i^{-1}$ agree on parts of $\tau=\pi\wedge\sigma$. Assuming this does
hold, we choose elements $u_i$ and $v_i$ such that $u_i$ is constant on
parts of $\pi$ and $v_i$ constant on parts of $\sigma$, and such that
$u_iv_i=a_ib_i^{-1}$ for all $i$.

We claim that this can be done in $|G|^{|\pi\vee\sigma|}$ ways, where $|\rho|$
denotes the number of parts of $\rho$.
